etymologies.etymologyHTML: From Middle English submitten, borrowed from Latin submittere, infinitive of submittō (“place under, yield”), from sub (“under, from below, up”) + mitto (“to send”). Compare upsend.

definitions.definition: (intransitive) To yield or give way to another.
(transitive) To yield (something) to another, as when defeated.
(transitive, intransitive) To enter or put forward for approval, consideration, marking etc.

quote.citation: 1843, Thomas Macaulay, Sir James Mackintosh's History of the Revolution:
quote.text: We submit that a wooden spoon of our day would not be justified in calling Galileo and Napier blockheads because they never heard of the differential calculus.

quote.citation: 2020 September 23, Paul Bigland, “The tragic tale of the Tay Bridge disaster”, in Rail, page 82:
quote.text: Determined to learn from Bouch's mistakes, they conducted a through [sic] survey of the riverbed. Having learned what they needed to know, they submitted plans for a new double-track bridge by the end of 1880.

definitions.definition: (transitive) To subject; to put through a process.

quote.text: [Skins] must be submitted to several washings, treadings, and stretchings, before they acquire the necessary pliancy.

definitions.definition: (transitive, mixed martial arts, professional wrestling) To win a fight against (an opponent) by submission.

quote.citation: Okamoto, Brett (2013 December 28) “Ronda Rousey wins with arm bar”, in ESPN.com‎[1], retrieved January 6, 2014
quote.text: "[Ronda] Rousey, a former U.S. Olympian in Judo, caps off a perfect year in which she submitted Liz Carmouche in the first-ever UFC female fight and coached opposite [Miesha] Tate in "The Ultimate Fighter" reality series."

quote.citation: Beaston, Erik (2022 February 19) “WWE Elimination Chamber 2022 Results: Winners, Grades, Reaction and Highlights”, in Bleacher Report‎[2], retrieved February 22, 2022
quote.text: "It was also the first time Goldberg has been submitted, enhancing Reigns even more than he already has been over the last two years."

definitions.definition: (transitive, obsolete) To let down; to lower.

quote.citation: 1662, John Dryden, Poem to the Lord Chancellor Hyde:
quote.text: Sometimes the hill submits itself a while.

definitions.definition: (transitive, obsolete) To put or place under.

quote.text: The bristled throat / Of the submitted sacrifice with ruthless steel he cut.
